title: OpenAI adds invisible text watermarking for EU ChatGPT and Codex
dek: A machine-readable watermark called textGrain is rolling out to EU users of ChatGPT and Codex as part of compliance with the EU AI Act.
body:
OpenAI has started adding an invisible, machine-readable watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union. The watermarking system is called textGrain and is being rolled out to meet requirements tied to the EU AI Act.

## Why it matters

The move puts OpenAI among the first major AI companies to deploy automatic text watermarking in production at scale. Watermarks are intended to help platforms, regulators, and tools identify AI-generated content without altering what humans see. OpenAI says textGrain performed as well as or better than other approaches, which has implications for how companies will meet regulatory obligations and for downstream detection tools.

## The details

- OpenAI is deploying an invisible, machine-readable watermark to text output from ChatGPT and Codex.
- The watermark rollout is limited to users in the European Union at first, linked to the EU AI Act rules.
- OpenAI calls its watermarking system textGrain.
- OpenAI says textGrain "matched or exceeded" other approaches such as Google DeepMind’s SynthID for text.
- The same SynthID approach served as the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August.

Many operational specifics are not yet public. OpenAI has not disclosed technical details about how textGrain embeds the watermark, the exact detection process, rates of false positives or negatives, or whether users will see controls or labels in the interface. The company also has not given a timetable for expanding watermarking beyond EU users.

## What to watch

Watch for technical documentation or independent tests that show how reliably textGrain can be detected and how it behaves across different prompts, languages, and downstream edits. Also track whether OpenAI expands the feature outside the EU and whether other providers adopt compatible or competing watermark schemes.
